prompt.en: A Basic-only operator without honours is offered two ways to use 29.62 MHz: a repeater whose output is on 29.62 MHz, or a direct simplex contact on 29.62 MHz. What prediction follows from the lesson's two privilege rules?

text.en: Both are treated alike because every 29.62 MHz amateur transmission is above the Basic-only boundary.
The repeater-output case can fit the bank's Basic-only repeater exception, but the simplex contact still falls below the 30 MHz gate.
The simplex contact is allowed because it is not automatic, but the repeater is barred until the operator holds Advanced.
Neither case can ever fit Basic-only operation because 29.62 MHz is below 30 MHz.

explanation.en: This is the repeater exception reconciled with the below-30-MHz gate. The bank names Basic-only use of repeaters starting at 29.500 MHz output, but that does not turn every below-30-MHz simplex contact into a Basic-only privilege.

prompt.en: Rank these maximum bandwidth settings from narrowest regulatory limit to widest: 10.12 MHz, 14.2 MHz, 29.6 MHz, and 146 MHz.

text.en: 10.12 MHz, then 14.2 MHz, then 29.6 MHz, then 146 MHz
14.2 MHz, then 10.12 MHz, then 146 MHz, then 29.6 MHz
29.6 MHz, then 14.2 MHz, then 10.12 MHz, then 146 MHz
146 MHz, then 29.6 MHz, then 14.2 MHz, then 10.12 MHz

explanation.en: The special 10.100 MHz to 10.150 MHz band is less than 6 kHz, the 7 MHz to 25 MHz group such as 14.2 MHz uses 6 kHz, 29.6 MHz is in the 20 kHz 10-metre range, and 146 MHz is in the 30 kHz 2-metre range.

prompt.en: Spot the error in this SSB troubleshooting note: 'The PEP meter is below the Basic limit, so a distorted voice report cannot be a regulatory problem; raise microphone gain until the other station hears you.'

text.en: The note treats the PEP limit as if it replaces the separate overmodulation control and 100% voice-modulation ceiling.
The note should say that SSB has no peak-envelope power limit at all.
The note should solve distorted voice reports by switching to an unmodulated carrier for the contact.
The note's only error is that Basic stations must always use Advanced SSB power limits.

explanation.en: Power and modulation quality are separate checks. Staying under the SSB PEP limit does not waive the requirement for means to prevent or indicate overmodulation or the 100% voice-modulation maximum.
